_doc: Intake questionnaire. The agent asks these in plain words (one screen, multiple choice where options exist) and records the answers with intake.py --answers; the user never types flags. Every answer is stored as given; 'unknown' or a skipped question becomes an open question in the report, never a guess. sets: the assessment.json fields each answer drives (documented here, applied in intake.py). when: ask only if another answer has this value.

questions.ask: What does the client want from this move to AWS?

options.label: Move it as it is
options.help: Same servers and operating systems on AWS (Windows to Windows, Linux to Linux). No code rewrite; only what must change to run on AWS.

options.label: Move and modernize
options.help: Update the code to run on Linux / modern .NET and move it to AWS.

options.label: Not decided yet
options.help: Plan the modernization and cost the move-as-is option next to it.

questions.ask: Which operating systems do the servers run today?

options.label: Not known yet
options.help: Becomes an open question for the client.

questions.ask: Where do the servers run today, and who manages them?
questions.example: Proxmox on-premises, managed by a vendor

questions.ask: What should happen to the database engine?

options.label: Keep the same engine
options.help: For example SQL Server stays SQL Server. No database code change.

options.label: Move to PostgreSQL
options.help: Convert the database and its code; SQL Server is removed.

options.label: Support both
options.help: The applications run on SQL Server and on PostgreSQL.

options.label: Decide later
options.help: Keep the engine for now; the report still shows the PostgreSQL options side by side.

questions.ask: Where will the databases run on AWS?

options.label: On EC2 servers we manage
options.help: Same as today, on AWS virtual machines. SQL Server features that Amazon RDS does not support keep working.

options.label: Amazon RDS (managed)
options.help: Some SQL Server features are limited on RDS; the report flags them.

questions.ask: Replace some servers with AWS managed services (for example SFTP to AWS Transfer Family, SMTP to Amazon SES, Kafka to Amazon MSK or SQS)?

options.label: Later
options.help: List the options as future work in the report, outside the estimate.

options.label: Yes, now
options.help: Include the code changes in the estimate.

questions.ask: How much of the code do we have access to?

options.label: Only some repositories
options.help: Assess these and estimate the rest of the estate from them.

questions.ask: How many repositories are in the whole estate (including the ones we cannot see)?
Is there a list of all the repositories (a CSV, Excel or JSON file)? Give its path.
Any compliance rules or data-location limits? (optional)
questions.example: PCI DSS; data must stay in the EU

questions.ask: How many engineers will do the work, and from what date do they have code access? (optional)
